name: lwtools
desc: Cross-development tools for Motorola 6809 and Hitachi 6309
why: Assembler and linker for the Motorola 6809 and Hitachi 6309 CPUs; a retro toolchain with a real hook, though deprecated.

brief.what_it_is: LWTOOLS is a set of cross-development tools for the Motorola 6809 and Hitachi 6309 microprocessors. The main piece is lwasm, an assembler that takes 6809/6309 assembly source and writes raw binaries, CoCo LOADM binaries, or a proprietary object file format for later linking. lwlink combines those object files, and the package also includes lwar (an archiver), lwcc-cpp, and lwobjdump. The homepage says the assembler supports macros and file inclusion, among other things.
brief.why_it_exists: The author, William Astle, started it in 2006 because none of the cross-assemblers available at the time supported all the features he wanted to use.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage gives no internals beyond the output targets. Source goes through lwasm, which emits raw, CoCo LOADM, or its own object format. Object files are then combined by lwlink. The homepage does not describe the object format or the linker's internals.

commands_seen.context: Run at the top level of the source directory to build lwtools on a reasonable system; binaries land in the lwasm, lwlink, and lwar directories.
Option to lwasm that returns forward-reference handling to its original behaviour; the 4.14 notes say forwardrefmax is on by default.
Flag (added in 4.22) that suppresses warnings about the use of ifp1.
Mentioned in the 4.3 notes as a command-line switch for setting symbol values; the page gives no exact syntax.

brief.install_notes: Build from source with make at the top level, then make install to put the binaries in /usr/local/bin/. Windows binaries can be built with mingw (using the MSYS shell, with the C drive at /c) or Cygwin with GCC or Clang and make. Visual Studio 2013-or-later project files are provided as an unsupported courtesy from 4.12 on. Prebuilt Windows binaries exist, including Tormod's in contrib/tormod and others in contrib/lw, and the 4.25 release ships win32 and win64 binaries that 'may or may not work'. No brew-specific notes appear on the homepage.
brief.standout: The project is a single-author retro toolchain that still gets roll-up releases and whose manual is published as HTML and PDF. The author openly takes donations and offers to implement features for a 'sufficient bribe'. The homepage also includes a dated changelog that records each release's breaking changes, such as the forwardrefmax default change in 4.14.
brief.status: Maintained, by the homepage's own evidence. The latest release is LWTOOLS 4.25, dated 2026-07-18, and the page says it was last modified Saturday, July 18, 2026. Before that came 4.24 (2025-04-18) and 4.23 (2024-08-03). The scout note calls the project 'deprecated', but the homepage does not say that anywhere.
brief.caveats: Windows support is shaky and unofficial: the author has said he cannot test Windows builds, the 4.25 Windows binaries 'may or may not work', and third-party binaries are unsupported. The Visual Studio projects are not officially supported. Bug reports for old releases are not wanted, and the page calls them 'provided for archaeological purposes only'. The 4.3 release is marked 'Don't use this release'. Some 4.12 error-detection fixes will break code that previously assembled, and the author says that code 'was working purely accidentally'. The 4.22 notes say the default optimization flag was lowered to -O2 because some compilers generated bad code under -O3. The homepage does not state a license.
quotes: LWTOOLS is a set of cross-development tools for the Motorola 6809 and Hitachi 6309 microprocessors.
LWTOOLS was born in 2006 when William Astle decided that none of the crossassemblers available at the time supported all the features he wanted to use.
Old releases are provided for archaeological purposes only.
If you have a pet feature you want added to the tools, you might be able to motivate me to implement it for a sufficient bribe.
